newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures cut losses late, end firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures cut losses late, end firm.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures cut losses late and finished afternoon range-trading barely firmer after swinging on both sides of even in busy morning activity.
Futures retreated to mostly lower levels during the second half of the day, still under pressure from a drop in U.S. Treasury bond futures.
But a bout of shortcovering tugged most units back up toward the plus side near the final bell.
"We sort of drifted higher," said one floor broker of closing trade. "It was a choppy day on some heavy volume, but we just couldn't find any direction, (had) no followthrough."
But the broker added that the ability of stock index futures to shake off pressure that spilled over from T-bonds could be technically and psychologically constructive.
"If you can't sell off, with bonds down over half a point, I would view that as supportive," he said.

T-bond futures fell most during the morning when Federal Reserve governor Janet Yellen told Reuters the economy had entered an "inflationary danger zone" but that the outlook for inflation and growth was not completely clear.
Yellen called the labor market "quite tight" but said growth of overall worker compensation had remained moderate.
Traders said the remarks redoubled attention on the Thursday's and Friday's U.S. inflation figures.

August producer prices are expected to firm 0.1 percent overall and in the core rate, while consumer prices are seen gaining 0.2 percent in both measures. Retail sales are forecast up 0.7 percent and gaining 0.4 percent ex-autos.
Traders said they had factored in a 25-basis-point rate hike at the September 24 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"If they (PPI and CPI) come out lower than expected, the feeling is 50-50 over whether it (Fed) does anything at all," said a another stock index futures floor broker.
He also said many traders believed that if the Fed did not increase rates, it risked eroding its credibility during an election year.

Traders noted fund selling on Tuesday, and one commission house they said had bought between 1,500 and 2,000 September S&P 500s during Monday's rise was seen selling out some of those contracts at midmorning on Tuesday.
At the same time, they said whenever nearby S&P 500s approached the day's low, buyers stepped in.
"It feels really weak, but they just keep coming in here and buying it," said another floor broker after midday.
Volume in S&P 500s was estimated on the price boards at roughly 88,000 contracts, which included about 18,000 December contracts involved in the rollover, floor brokers said.
Fair value was roughly 0.40 point over cash. Arbitrage buy programs needed at least 1.10 points premium. Sell programs would have required about a 0.30-point discount.
September S&Ps early stalled at Monday's high of 665.20 but later rose above and then crossed back below that level.

Sept S&P 500s settled up 0.05 pt at 665.10, Midcap 400 fell 0.35 to 232.65, Value Lines up 0.50 pt at 622.50, NYSE Composite added 0.15 to 356.95, Nikkei rose 300.0 to 20,625.0. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
